rule: Prefer products with existing search demand when using Google-first acquisition
notes: Search-intent products let small traffic volumes matter.

rule: Optimize expected contribution profit per click, not revenue ROAS
notes: Formula: expected CVR * pre-ad contribution/order - CPC.

rule: For very low ad budgets, high-ticket/high gross-profit dollars per conversion are structurally easier
notes: Not universal; high AOV also raises trust/CVR requirements.

rule: Launch one country/market first rather than splitting tiny budgets
notes: Concentrates learning and makes data interpretable.

rule: Start with a lean, researched catalog rather than thousands of supplier SKUs
notes: Avoids diluted spend and simplifies feed/data quality.

rule: Treat Merchant Center feed as an acquisition surface: titles, GTIN, brand, category, images, price, shipping
notes: Run controlled item-level tests where possible.

rule: At tiny budgets, Standard Shopping/manual or constrained structures can be useful for collecting interpretable query/SKU data
notes: Evidence is mixed and platform behavior changes; test rather than dogmatize.

rule: Use PMax after sufficient clean conversion data and with brand/structure guardrails
notes: Avoid brand cannibalization and false ROAS confidence.

rule: Observe daily but avoid unnecessary early intervention
Scale proven profitable campaigns gradually rather than jumping budgets
notes: ~20% increments recur in operator playbooks, but treat as heuristic not law.

rule: Reconcile ad-platform revenue to store-side orders/revenue
notes: Branded search, retargeting and PMax can inflate platform ROAS.

rule: Track COGS, shipping, payment fees, returns/refunds and contribution profit daily
notes: Revenue and platform ROAS are insufficient.

rule: Use Google free listings + Bing free listings + Pinterest catalogs + SEO before paying for broad acquisition
notes: Free signals can prioritize which SKU/market deserves paid testing.

rule: If demand must be created, discovery channels can precede Google capture
notes: Existing-search-demand and demand-creation products need different playbooks.

rule: Log every intervention with before/after state, hypothesis and evaluation date
notes: Enables replay/causal analysis and prevents hindsight narratives.
